headline: High: slim can write and execute against container artifacts while PaddleOCR can ingest browser/API content, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt injection is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented between PaddleOCR and slim, so direct injection is not default. However, PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs, while slim executes shell commands and reads/writes files; if an operator manually pipes OCR output into slim, attacker-controlled text could influence commands. The pathway is possible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies PaddleOCR output into slim's interactive prompt or stdin
IF OCR output is treated as shell input or command text
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste boundary and never paste OCR text into shell prompts
Wrap slim invocations in a script that rejects non-command input
Review any OCR-derived text before passing it to slim
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred text

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted network egress; slim reads filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys, and has broad network egress. If both operate on the same workspace or container artifacts, sensitive file contents can flow from slim into PaddleOCR outputs or external APIs. The shared-workspace path is plausible, though not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or container image artifacts
IF PaddleOCR sends extracted content to an external API or browser endpoint
mitigations: Separate workspaces for OCR inputs and container-analysis artifacts
Remove secrets from any directory scanned by either agent
Disable external API calls during shared-data processing
Run a quick grep for private keys before invoking either agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR can call APIs and run browsers, while slim can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read and write the filesystem, and use broad network egress. Even though slim does not modify git state and PaddleOCR has no write capability listed, both can mutate shared files or external resources if aimed at the same target. The overlap is enough for write conflicts in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree or artifact set
IF either agent writes derived outputs back into a shared directory
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Make shared inputs read-only
Serialize runs so only one agent writes at a time
Check for file collisions before starting slim
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents and images, and slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands and processes filesystem artifacts. If an operator treats OCR output as authoritative and feeds it into slim-driven actions, OCR mistakes can cascade into incorrect container changes or analysis results. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the risk exists in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is used as the source of truth for slim commands or scripts
IF no human verification occurs between OCR extraction and shell execution
mitigations: Manually verify OCR output before acting on it
Use a diff or checksum against source documents
Keep slim in dry-run mode for first pass
Require a second reviewer for command-bearing OCR text
requires-engineering: add schema validation for OCR-to-command handoff

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR handles documents and images, while slim handles filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate private keys, and registry credentials. That combination can create compliance issues if regulated documents or secrets are processed together, especially because slim has broad network egress and PaddleOCR can call APIs. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents, PHI, or secrets are present in the shared workflow
IF either agent sends those materials to an external API or registry
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared runs
Redact secrets before processing
Confirm data residency before enabling network access
Log which files each agent touched
requires-engineering: add policy checks for sensitive data classes
